title: Introduction; small town life; childhood and schooling; courtship and marriage
description: The interview begins with an introduction of Olive Randall by Irma Wood. Olive discusses the benefits of living in a small town like St. Maries, her upbringing on a homestead near Sandpoint, and her education. She then talks about meeting her husband at a dance, their three-year courtship, and her views on marriage as a 50-50 partnership.

title: Childbirth and child rearing; family life and grandchildren; recreation and social activities
description: Olive describes the medical services available when she had her children, including going to hospitals in Sandpoint and St. Maries. She mentions learning about child rearing from her mother and older women, and talks about her children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren. Olive also discusses her recreational activities, such as belonging to lodges and clubs, and dancing at the senior citizens' center.

title: Homemaking and farm work; family responsibilities; community clubs and organizations
description: Olive talks about supporting her family through homemaking, raising a garden, and caring for livestock like cows, chickens, and horses. She describes the times when she had the major responsibility for her family while her husband worked in the timber. Olive also mentions her involvement in various community clubs, including the home demonstration club and the grandmothers' club, and their activities.

title: Senior citizens' club; logging and homestead life
description: Olive provides details about the senior citizens' club, including potluck dinners, dancing, printing a paper called The Sparkler, and fundraising efforts. She then recounts her experiences moving to a homestead cabin in the Alder Creek area for her husband's logging work, describing the journey by train and log train, and living there for nine years before moving back to St. Maries.
